standard.title: Curate and present visual arts practice
standard.description: curate and present examples of their visual arts practice to accompany exhibits of their artworks to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning to audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can present artworks with basic accompanying documentation (AC9AVA6P01). They have not yet made deliberate curation decisions about which works to present, how to organise them, or how documentation can connect artworks to ideas and meaning for an audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students curate and present examples of their visual arts practice with documentation that connects artworks to ideas, perspectives and meaning for a specific audience.

nodes.label: Understanding curation and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what curation involves and how curation choices affect what an audience understands about the artworks and the artist's ideas
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what curation involves; describe at least two decisions a curator makes and how each affects audience experience
nodes.typical_width: Investigate examples of curated exhibitions; analyse the curation decisions made (selection, arrangement, labelling, space) and explain how each shapes audience experience and understanding
wider: Visit and critically evaluate an exhibition in a gallery, museum or community site — analyse specific curation decisions and evaluate their effectiveness for the intended audience
Investigate how digital curation (webpage, walkthrough, online showcase) makes different choices than physical curation — analyse what each enables and constrains
Research how artists describe their artistic vision in exhibition contexts — analyse how language choices in labels and statements shape audience understanding

response_modes.reason: Students need exposure to multiple curation contexts — physical and digital, school and professional, different audience types — to understand that curation is a design practice with genuine decisions and consequences. A single example of a school display doesn't build the conceptual understanding needed for deliberate curation choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The gallery visit direction is genuinely rich — direct engagement with professional curation practices gives advancing students a concrete reference point that classroom examples cannot replicate. The digital curation direction also opens a genuinely different set of curation considerations that advance students' understanding of what presentation choices are available.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two curation decisions and explains how each affects audience experience
Does not treat presentation as merely displaying artworks — understands it as a communicative act

nodes.label: Creating documentation for artworks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create documentation (labels, statements, explanations) that connects their artworks to intended ideas, perspectives and meaning for an audience
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one piece of documentation (label, statement or explanation) for an artwork; documentation should connect the work to its intended ideas or meaning
nodes.typical_width: Create documentation for multiple artworks that communicates the ideas, perspectives and meaning behind each work to a specific audience; use visual arts terminology appropriately
wider: Research a variety of gallery label formats and develop own label that goes beyond basic identification to communicate artistic vision
Create an extended artist statement that articulates the ideas, processes and decisions behind a body of work
Develop documentation that uses different formats for different audience types — e.g. a technical statement for peers and an accessible explanation for younger students

response_modes.reason: Writing documentation that genuinely connects artworks to ideas — rather than just describing what they look like or how they were made — is a precision writing skill that develops through repeated practice with feedback. Students need to practise the specific move of articulating meaning rather than process, and this habit develops through iteration, not through broader documentation contexts.

Students commonly write documentation that describes the artwork ('I used blue because I like blue') rather than explaining the meaning ('I used blue to communicate the coldness and distance in the relationship depicted'). Scaffolding the reasoning distinction — what does this work communicate vs how was it made — builds the writing habit that makes documentation genuinely useful for audiences.

success_criteria: Creates documentation that connects artworks to intended ideas or meaning
Documentation goes beyond description — communicates meaning and artistic vision

nodes.label: Curating and presenting a coherent exhibition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make deliberate curation decisions about which works to present, how to arrange them, and how documentation supports the exhibition's communicative intent
nodes.minimum_width: Present at least one artwork with documentation in a chosen context; explain at least two curation decisions made and why
nodes.typical_width: Curate a selection of works for presentation; make deliberate decisions about selection, arrangement and documentation; explain how curation choices support the exhibition's communicative intent
wider: Create a themed series of artworks curated for display — use Viewpoints questions to guide decisions about visual narrative, spatial relationships and audience experience

Create a digital presentation (webpage, walkthrough) to connect geographically distanced audiences with a visual arts showcase — evaluate the specific curation decisions needed for digital presentation
Develop an exhibition that tells a story through the arrangement and relationships between works — document the curatorial thinking behind the visual narrative

response_modes.reason: This node integrates understanding of curation principles (Node 1), documentation writing skills (Node 2), and artwork creation from AC9AVA8C02 into a coherent presented exhibition. The coordination of selection, arrangement, documentation and communicative intent is the learning — students who can create artworks and write labels but cannot make the curation decisions that connect them into a coherent whole have not reached this node.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The visual narrative through curation direction — using Viewpoints to think about how groupings, spatial relationships and audience experience create meaning beyond individual artworks — is genuinely rich. Advancing students who engage here develop curatorial thinking as a distinct artistic practice, not just an administrative task.
success_criteria: Presents artworks with documentation in a chosen context
Makes and explains at least two deliberate curation decisions
Curation choices are connected to communicative intent — not just aesthetic preference
